title: Network Delay Time
summary: A signal starts at node k.

contractDetails.constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 100. There are 1–6000 directed links, with distinct ordered endpoint pairs, different endpoints in [1,n], and integer weights in [0,100].

statement: A signal starts at node k. Each row [from, to, travelTime] specifies a directed link. Return when the last node first receives the signal, or −1 if any node is unreachable.

examples.explanation: The route through node 3 reaches node 2 sooner than the direct link.
Two zero-time edges deliver the signal immediately.
Node 3 has no outgoing links and cannot reach the others.

constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 100. There are 1–6000 directed links, with distinct ordered endpoint pairs, different endpoints in [1,n], and integer weights in [0,100].
hints: Conceptual: Each node receives the signal along its fastest directed route.
Directional: Use Dijkstra’s algorithm to finalize the smallest tentative arrival time first.
Implementation: Relax only outgoing edges. Return −1 for any unreachable node, otherwise the maximum finalized distance.
complexityAnalysis: O(V² + E) time and O(V²) space with a weighted adjacency matrix and a scan for the next vertex.
